item: Row 432: no trigger or view a backup carries runs in the import; custody schema refusal and seal reasons by evidence
summary: The schema check of an imported corpus knew the names of the triggers and views the app makes, not their bodies: a backup could carry article_fts_au with any SQL in it, and it ran on the merge's country-code write and the newsletter filter's DELETE (shown with a planted body; the undisarmed control rewrites every merged title). staged_key.disarm_staged now drops every trigger and view from our staged copy once it is staged (reader) and again at the merge's own entry (idempotent), after the name check and before the newsletter filter, the upgrade, the walk and the merge; nothing the merge reads from inc is maintained by those triggers (its search index and per-day tables are not carried), and an ordinary backup merges to the same working copy with and without the drop (tested). A text allowlist was rejected: older builds wrote other trigger texts (fts.py has 46 versions), so it would refuse good backups. Residual on the merge connection: CHECK, DEFAULT, generated-column and index expressions of the staged schema, able to call only the search index's four normalisers (oo_fts_norm, oo_fts_used, oo_fts_caps, oo_search_fold) and oo_inc_feed_key, all pure, with load_extension refused (a test lists the host's functions against an allowlist); trusted_schema stays on there because the working copy's own triggers call registered functions. A custody log refused for its schema on the sealing path (A2) is now left out and the import goes on, in the merge's own words, as on the keyed path (A1). The seal's refusal is chosen by evidence, never by the driver's words: SQLite's result code, the disk's free space against what the copy still needs (sqlcipher_export reports a full disk as SQLITE_ERROR, measured), and a zero-timeout lock probe; a disk without room for the copy is refused before a byte is written.
